items.q: How is this different from a marketing agency?
items.a: A marketing agency sells impressions, clicks, or rankings. We sell booked patient visits and service-line revenue — every deliverable is scoped to a growth metric on your P&L, not a marketing dashboard. If a channel isn't hitting cost-per-booked-visit, we cut it, not defend it.

items.q: What does the first 90 days look like?
items.a: Days 1–30: diagnostic, baseline, growth model, and funnel rebuild. Days 31–60: booking-flow tuning, SEO + local live, review engine launched. Days 61–90: paid channels live at cost-per-booked-visit targets, referral outreach kicked off, and the first monthly executive report shipped.

items.q: Do you work with multi-location practices?
items.a: Yes — this is a core specialty. We build per-location P&L, per-clinic marketing budgets, provider-level utilization tracking, and centralized brand governance so no clinic drifts off-brand or off-budget.

Yes. Every automation, integration, and review flow runs on BAA-covered infrastructure. Response templates never reference PHI, and we audit any existing widgets, forms, and PMS integrations for exposure before we touch them.

items.q: Do you integrate with our practice management system?
items.a: We integrate with the major dermatology PMS platforms — Nextech, ModMed, EMA, AdvancedMD — for attribution and reporting. Where deep integration isn't possible, we set up conversion tracking at the booking layer so no visit is uncounted.

items.q: What happens if a channel underperforms?
items.a: We cut it. Every channel has a monthly cost-per-booked-visit ceiling agreed upfront. If a channel exceeds that ceiling two months in a row without a clear seasonality reason, budget rotates into a channel that's hitting target — no defensive reporting, no sunk-cost pitches.
